home.title: A reusable foundation for PHP applications
home.lead: A reusable PHP, Slim, and Vue foundation serving a website and API from one deployment.
home.intro: Explore its layered structure, protected sessions, JSON API, Vite frontend, explicit migrations, and checks. Auth and Posts are working examples you can extend.
home.repositoryLink: View the sandbox_php repository on GitHub
home.featuresText: The foundation separates HTTP adapters, application operations, domain rules, persistence, and dependency wiring. Auth and the Posts blog demonstrate those capabilities in a working application.
home.featureList: Server-side sessions with login regeneration, CSRF protection, and backend ownership checks.|Vue 3 and Vue Router source compiled by Vite into production assets.|JSON API with an OpenAPI reference in local environments.|Explicit Phinx migrations and focused, integration, architecture, and browser checks.
home.stackText: The backend uses PHP 8.4, Slim 4, PDO/MySQL, and Phinx. The frontend uses Vue 3, Vue Router, Tailwind CSS, shadcn-vue, and Lucide, built with Vite. PHP continues to serve the page and API, and browser API requests use the same PHP origin.
home.stackEnvironment: During development, run the PHP app and Vite together; Vite serves transformed modules and HMR. Install frontend dependencies with npm. Production assets are compiled beneath public/assets/build/; the optional Docker example serves them with Nginx, and shared hosting serves them with Apache. Runtime images do not need Node.js.
home.frontendWorkflow: Run these commands from the project root. The PHP app must also be running during development so pages and same-origin API requests work.
home.frontendCommandsLabel: Frontend install, development, build, and test commands
home.frontendCommands:
npm --prefix frontend ci
npm --prefix frontend run dev
npm --prefix frontend run build
npm --prefix frontend run test
home.productionAssets: Run the frontend build before building or deploying production. It writes the Vite manifest and compiled assets to public/assets/build/; Nginx serves them in the optional Docker example, and Apache serves them on shared hosting.
home.architectureText: HTTP controllers call Application services, which use Domain entities and repository contracts. PDO implementations live in Infrastructure; Bootstrap connects dependencies and registers routes. Controllers adapt HTTP and contain no SQL. Repositories persist data without deciding business rules.
home.architecturePaths: src/Domain/User and src/Domain/Post: rules, invariants, and contracts.|src/Application: application operations without Slim or PDO.|src/Infrastructure: controllers, sessions, Markdown, and MySQL repositories.|src/Bootstrap: configuration, composition, and routes.|frontend/src: Vue SPA and API source; public/assets/build: compiled frontend output.|database/migrations and tests: versioned schema and checks.
home.architectureExtension: To add a domain, create its contracts and implementations in their respective layers and connect them in Bootstrap.
home.installText: Create a new project with Composer in an empty destination, initialize a fresh Git repository, then start the development app with Docker Compose. Replace the example credentials first. Open http://localhost:8080 after setup.
home.installMigration: Migrations use Phinx and are never applied at startup. Run composer migrate explicitly, then composer migrate:status to inspect the result.
home.installEnvironment: Keep the real .env out of version control. The project is published on Packagist; its current version is dev-main, so include --stability=dev when creating it. Run later Composer commands in the active app container when the setup instructions call for them.
home.auth: Registration, login, and the Posts workflow
home.authList: Open Login and follow the registration link to create an account.|Sign in; the menu shows My Posts and Log out.|In My Posts, create a draft with a title and Markdown.|Review the preview, save, and publish. The published Post appears in the Blog.|Edit, unpublish, or delete only Posts owned by your account.
home.authSecurity: Passwords are stored as hashes. The session is regenerated at login, authenticated mutations require CSRF, and the backend checks ownership for each operation. This demo has no password recovery or attempt limit; define recovery and abuse controls before exposing a derived application publicly.
home.routesText: The JSON API is described by OpenAPI. In local development, /docs serves Swagger UI and the reference when OPENAPI_ENABLED is true; the production configuration disables it by default. Regenerate docs/openapi.json from PHP route attributes with the command below.
home.routesList: /: introduction and documentation.|/blog and /blog/{slug}: public reading of published Posts.|/login and /register: authentication.|/my-posts: editor for the signed-in user's Posts.|/api/auth/*, /api/posts*, and /api/me/posts*: session, reading, and editing API.|/docs: Swagger UI and OpenAPI when enabled.
home.qualityText: Run the Vitest frontend suite and PHPUnit directly; neither needs a browser, running PHP application, database, or container. Each test suite has a 20-second CI limit.
home.qualityCommands: Choose checks for the change. Format writes files; lint checks style and syntax; test runs PHPUnit; quality adds coverage, PHPStan, and OpenAPI checks.
home.qualityDetails: migrate:status reports migration state without applying changes. npm --prefix frontend run test checks selected frontend behavior with mocked dependencies; composer test runs the service-free PHPUnit suite.
home.securityText: compose.prod.yaml is an optional VPS/adopter example with Nginx and private PHP-FPM; only Nginx publishes HTTP. It has not been fully validated in a real target environment, so adopters must validate their proxy/TLS, secrets, firewall, persistence, and backup setup. This is separate from the active Apache shared-hosting release path. Use an environment file outside the repository, set your own secrets, APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, OPENAPI_ENABLED=false, and a public HTTPS APP_URL. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy and do not expose MySQL. Back up the database before upgrades and apply migrations as a controlled step.
home.securityCookie: The session cookie receives Secure when the public URL uses HTTPS. Keep environment files and database backups outside the public directory. Registration is open, and this demo has no password recovery or rate limiting; assess and implement those controls before publishing a derived application.
home.securityVue: Vue templates are compiled by Vite before deployment. Do not accept user-provided Vue templates or executable HTML. Markdown preview escapes raw HTML and blocks unsafe links.
home.customizationText: Adapt User fields and Auth flows to the derived product. Preserve password hashing, secure sessions, login session regeneration, CSRF, and backend authorization. Keep rules in Domain, orchestration in Application, and integrations in Infrastructure; connect dependencies and routes in Bootstrap.
home.customizationModel: When changing the data model, coordinate updates to the entity, repository contract, PDO implementation, API, and tests. Add a new migration for an existing installation instead of editing an applied migration.
home.customizationDomain: For a new domain, keep rules in Domain, orchestration in Application, and integrations in Infrastructure. Register dependencies and routes in Bootstrap. Prefer focused contracts over generic extension abstractions; current source and tests contain examples.
home.customizationGuideLink: Read the User/Auth customization and domain extension guide
home.sddText: SDD Lite is an optional, separately maintained workflow. It is not needed to install or run this application.
home.sddDetails: Feature records use feature.md, spec.md, plan.md, and review.md. Historical records may retain their original format.
home.sddStart: Invoke $sdd-lite with a command such as feature, spec, plan, code, or review. Read the skill instructions for its usage.

home.hostingText: The optional Docker example uses compose.prod.yaml behind a TLS reverse proxy; it is intended for adopters and has not been fully validated on a real VPS. The repository's active release path is Apache shared hosting, with public/ as the document root and src/, vendor/, and .env outside it. Either deployment needs a database backup before upgrades and an explicit, controlled migration.
home.hostingGuide: Read the full Docker and shared-hosting setup and deployment instructions
home.sddLink: Visit the canonical SDD Lite project and current installation instructions
home.composerDocs: Read the official Composer create-project documentation
home.openApiRoute: Open the API reference at /docs when enabled
home.installCommands:
composer create-project --stability=dev paulobezerra/sandbox-php my-project --remove-vcs
cd my-project
git init
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env and replace the example passwords.
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose exec -T app composer migrate
docker compose exec -T app composer migrate:status
